PullRequest.Title: Add a consistent empty state to the Agents Search tab
PullRequest.Body:
Fixes #334630

## Summary

Give the Agents Window Search tab the same empty-state treatment as the other tabs, instead of leaving the results area blank.

- Reuse the shared Sessions heading and description: **Search** / **Search for text in your files**.
- Keep the contribution entirely in the Sessions layer; regular VS Code Search is unchanged.
- Follow the current results model and layout, preserving query controls, populated results, the existing “No Results” text, and restored-query messages. The empty state adds no tab stops and does not intercept pointer input or move focus.
- Add six real-editor regression tests and extend the real Search editor fixtures with empty, compact, narrow, populated, no-results, and restored-query states.

## Validation

- **9 targeted tests passed in Chromium and Electron**, including the existing Sessions editor/empty-state tests.
- Client typecheck, targeted ESLint/import-layer checks, stylelint, and commit hygiene passed.
- Verified nine empty-state fixtures across dark, light, and dark high contrast; confirmed centering, containment, and unchanged query controls. Also checked populated/no-results/restored-query fixtures, query-clearing preservation, and native Tab through the query controls.
- Visual and interaction validation used real-component browser fixtures, not a full desktop walkthrough.

## Manual testing

1. Open a new Search tab in the Agents Window. The heading and description should be centered below the query controls.
2. Run searches with and without matches. Existing results and “No Results” should replace the initial empty state. Clearing the query must not hide existing results.
3. Check compact/narrow layouts and high-contrast themes; navigate the query controls using Tab. The empty-state text must not introduce a focus stop.

Scenarios.Scenario: Open the Agents Window with ordinary code editors, query editors, and other embedded editors
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The new module is loaded with the Sessions search contribution, and the contribution is instantiated for each code editor after first render during idle time (or within the framework's 50 ms fallback). It is not on the initial-render critical path.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number of simultaneously instantiated code editors in the Agents Window; contribution construction is once per editor.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Each editor schedules its own idle callback; contribution construction and listener registration execute synchronously on the renderer thread, without a new queue or parallel boundary.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: observableCodeEditor uses a process-local map keyed by editor, so an existing facade is reused; on a cold editor it creates one facade, while later requests are warm. The map entry and listeners are removed when the editor is disposed.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: registration is global to code editors in the Sessions bundle and AfterFirstRender semantics are explicit; the actual work and lifecycle are directly visible.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: The number of embedded editors varies, but the added per-editor work is bounded to one contribution/autorun and reuse of a cached observable facade; no heavyweight model, I/O, serialization, or DOM subtree is created for non-search models.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. There is small eager per-editor bookkeeping, but it is deferred beyond first render, bounded, cached, disposed with editor lifetime, and lacks a concrete user-visible performance outcome.

Scenarios.Scenario: Open or restore a Sessions Search editor with empty, populated, no-results, or restored content
Scenarios.CriticalPath: After the search result model is attached, the autorun reads the model scheme and O(1) value length. Only an empty SearchEditor model synchronously creates a three-element empty-state DOM subtree and one overlay; populated/no-results models do not create it.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Existing workspace text search initiated by SearchModel.search(query), potentially backed by filesystem, process, or remote search services.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One existing logical search operation per debounced query submission; result cardinality is serialized by existing SearchEditor code.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same SearchModel.search operation and result-model update occurred before the diff; only the empty-state overlay was absent.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The existing search must complete before result text is committed, but the new contribution only observes the committed model version and does not initiate, await, duplicate, or fan out the search.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Existing persisted Search editor model resolution/revert may read a saved search file or working-copy backup.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most one existing resolve/read for the SearchEditor input being opened or reverted.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Opening/restoring resolved the same model and backing content before the diff.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Model resolution remains required before restoration; the new observer runs only after model attachment and adds no read.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Search-result model content changes. The observer runs once per version change, performs a constant-time length check, and creates/removes one fixed-size overlay only when transitioning through empty content.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Search submissions remain coalesced by the existing RunOnceScheduler/delayer and existing search cancellation. Empty-state updates are synchronous reactive callbacks on model changes and introduce no additional concurrency.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The observable editor facade is shared per editor. The overlay is retained only while the current SearchEditor model is empty and is disposed on content/model change or contribution/editor disposal; there is no result cache or retained history.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the model/version dependencies, scheme guard, fixed DOM creation, and disposal through reader.store are explicit, and the existing search boundary call path was inspected.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Search result sizes and providers vary, but the diff does not alter search cardinality, result serialization, or boundary traffic; its incremental work remains constant per model event.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. The change adds only bounded constant-time observation and a fixed DOM subtree, without increasing existing search I/O, serialization, or concurrency.

Scenarios.Scenario: Resize or relayout an empty Sessions Search results editor
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The existing SearchEditor layout synchronously computes query/results dimensions; after the editor emits its layout event, the new nested autorun writes the already-provided width and height to the overlay styles. This is on the resize/layout path but performs no geometry read.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: One pair of style writes per emitted editor layout event while the results model is empty; independent of workspace size and search-result count.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Fully synchronous on the renderer thread and serialized with editor layout events; no timers, tasks, or fan-out are added.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The layout observer exists only while the empty overlay exists and is disposed when content becomes non-empty, the model changes, or the contribution is disposed.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: layoutInfo is event-backed and the callback only assigns CSS width/height; the overlay CSS uses flex centering without queried geometry.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Resize event frequency depends on user interaction, but the changed callback has fixed work and does not force a read-after-write layout cycle in the traced code.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. The resize work is bounded, scoped to the empty state, and does not establish forced synchronous layout or dropped-frame risk.

Analysis.Summary: Reviewed all six changed files and traced global editor-contribution instantiation, SearchEditor model/search flow, overlay lifecycle, and resize behavior. No high-confidence actionable performance regression was introduced, and the PR does not fix a traced prior performance regression.
